title: New Tariffs Could Make Shopping More Expensive
summary:
The Trump administration plans a new round of tariffs. Tariffs are taxes on goods from other countries, and they could raise prices for shoppers. The plan covers China, the European Union, and 12 other trading partners.

China would face the highest rate: a new 20 percent tariff on most products. That could add up to 40 percent in total if talks fall apart. Others would face 10 to 20 percent more. The new tariffs could start as soon as January.

Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the goal is to protect American manufacturing. He said America should make more of what it uses. The tariffs would apply to only some goods, the administration says.

Wall Street Journal reporter Gavin Bade said they would matter a lot for shoppers. The Yale Economic Lab estimated they would add about $400 for each American. In February, the Supreme Court ruled many earlier tariffs illegal. This time, it is using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. Bade said this approach is more likely to stand up in court.
why_it_matters: Tariffs can make the things your family buys cost more, so this plan could change what shopping costs.
